svg.title: Gina vs Go net/http HTTP/2 benchmark results
svg.desc: Six small charts comparing Gina (shard threads in one process) with Go net/http serving HTTP/2 on 1 to 8 cores: keep-alive throughput over h2c and h2 over TLS, a 64 KiB echo test, p99 latency over both, and memory use. Gina is faster on every throughput and latency measure; its 4- and 8-core points are probably limited by the load generator. Gina uses more memory than net/http at 8 cores. The same numbers are tabulated in docs/BENCHMARKS.md.
svg.text: HTTP/2 only on both sides. Same cores, same routes, same bodies. Loopback, 64 connections x 4 streams, median of two 4 s runs per point.
Server pinned to N physical cores; the oha load generator runs on separate cores. Gina: one process, N pinned shard threads (Tina's model).

g.text: Requests per second (thousands) · higher is better
Keep-alive GET, h2 over TLS: 4.0–6.5× throughput
Requests per second (thousands) · higher is better
POST /echo, requests per second (thousands) · higher is better
Keep-alive GET, milliseconds · lower is better
Keep-alive GET, milliseconds · lower is better
Resident memory of the server process (MB) · lower is better

svg.text: Gina's 4- and 8-core points are probably limited by the load generator (4 to 8 cores adds only 6%), so those ratios are lower bounds.
Not a feature-equal comparison: net/http is a complete, hardened server; Gina's HTTP/2 has no push, priorities or trailers, and its TLS 1.3 is unaudited.
Shard threads share one Go heap and GC. One machine (AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395), Go 1.26, oha 1.16, 2026-10-07. Tables and caveats: docs/BENCHMARKS.md.
